subject: SpectraWorks capacity claim — reconciliation & temporary tranche plan
messages:
From: Alice Lee <alice.lee@spectraworks.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: john.connor@spectraworks.com, procurement@spectraworks.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: unexpected capacity encroachment impacting SpectraWorks SLA

Hi Karthik,

Quick summary — over the past 48 hours we've seen a sustained 35% reduction in our provisioned throughput on the Dedicated pool tied to SPECT-4392 during peak hours (US-PST). This is causing timeouts in our inference pipelines and we're getting escalations from product teams. Our monitoring shows large, unanticipated batch jobs from other customers running into the same tranche region.

We need two things: 1) confirmation of whether Redwood is applying any dynamic preemption or rebalancing for Dedicated customers that would explain this; 2) a short-term mitigation plan (24-72 hrs) so we can meet our internal SLAs while procurement finalizes the reserved capacity commit.

I've attached a brief log/metrics export and timeline. Can we get an owner on this?

Thanks,
Alice Lee
Head of ML Ops — SpectraWorks
alice.lee@spectraworks.com

Attachments: spectra_capacity_claim_summary.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alice Lee <alice.lee@spectraworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: unexpected capacity encroachment impacting SpectraWorks SLA

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the data. I'm escalating and will coordinate a temporary tranche for you.

High level: Dedicated customers can be affected by transient preemption when we apply cluster-level rebalancing for emergency maintenance or when we trigger cross-deal burst protections. That said, your account should not be seeing >30% degradation on a sustained basis.

Immediate next steps (24 hours):
- I'm asking Vivek (infra ops) to do an emergency assert on tranche assignment and any active preemption logs.
- Marissa will collaborate with our allocation team to propose a temporary reserved tranche that pins your queues for the next 72 hours.
- Ben will surface the relevant contract language regarding interim compensation/credits if we determine an SLA miss.

Can you confirm which time window is most critical for you (PST peak hours)? If you can share a 2-3 hour window we will prioritize that slot for the temporary tranche.

Karthik
Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: unexpected capacity encroachment impacting SpectraWorks SLA

FYI — initial check of the allocation logs shows a scheduled cross-cluster kernel rollout that kicked off 2026-10-27 23:45 UTC. The rollout included opportunistic live-migration steps which may have allowed transient batch jobs to land on the neighbouring tranche before migration completed. I'm pulling the detailed preemption traces now.

Preliminary ask for SpectraWorks: provide the most critical 2-hour PST window. I can carve a temp tranche (8 GPUs equivalent) isolated by QoS label for 48-72 hours, but we will need a short maintenance window to drain in-flight KV caches before pinning which could cause a 5-7 minute cold start.

I'll post the exact trace export once it's ready.

-Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime Ops
From: Alice Lee <alice.lee@spectraworks.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: john.connor@spectraworks.com, procurement@spectraworks.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: unexpected capacity encroachment impacting SpectraWorks SLA

Thanks Karthik/Vivek — critical window is 14:00–16:00 PST (peak inference traffic for production pipelines). A 5–7 minute cold start is acceptable as long as the tranche is isolated and we get confirmation when it is pinned.

Procurement: we'll also need a written note about any temporary credits if there is an SLA determination.

Alice
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alice Lee <alice.lee@spectraworks.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary tranche plan & next steps (v1)

Alice — attaching a first-pass temporary tranche plan and allocation matrix for the 72-hour window. Key points:
- We propose pinning 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs from 14:00–16:00 PST daily for the next 3 days (2026-10-29 to 2026-10-31) to match your stated peak.
- During the pinned window we'll disable cross-deal bursting into that tranche and enforce cache-isolation labels. Expected cold-start penalty ~6 minutes once at the start of the pinned period.
- After the 72-hour window we will evaluate metrics and either extend the tranche or transition you to a formal reserved tranche posture while procurement finalizes SPECT-4392.

Files: temp_tranche_plan_v1.xlsx; allocation_matrix_20261102.csv

Action items for SpectraWorks: please acknowledge acceptance of the plan and sign off on the 6-minute cold-start acceptable. Procurement to confirm that the procurement team has visibility into the potential credit discussion.

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: John Connor <john.connor@spectraworks.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Lee <alice.lee@spectraworks.com>, procurement@spectraworks.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary tranche plan & next steps (v1)

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for isolating the tranche. SpectraWorks accepts the 72-hour plan and the cold-start tradeoff. Procurement confirms they will open a short ticket to discuss credit if SLA breach is confirmed; I'll loop them into the HubSpot record HS-201234567.

Please proceed with the pinning for today 14:00–16:00 PST. We'll monitor and report any anomalies.

John Connor
VP, Platform Engineering — SpectraWorks

Forwarded-For-Records: procurement@spectraworks.com
